newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. aide hopes Iraq oil deal can go ahead.
newsitem.headline: U.N. aide hopes Iraq oil deal can go ahead.

text.p: United Nations Under-Secretary General Yasushi Akashi said on Monday he hoped the Iraq "oil-for-food" deal could go ahead in the near future.
Akashi told a news conference the world body was currently assessing whether all conditions had been met for the suspended deal to be put into force.
"We hope that in the near future.....we shall be able to do it," said Akashi, a top aide to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
Under the deal, signed last May, Iraq would be permitted to sell $2 billion of oil over six months with the proceeds going partly towards meeting humanitarian needs.
But implementation was suspended this month when Iraqi President Saddam Hussein moved troops to the north of the country to help one side in fighting between Kurdish factions.
"The majority of people in Iraq are living below the poverty line, and recent military action has made the situation worse," Akashi said.
He said the U.N., which has relief officials in northern Iraq in Kurdish-controlled areas, was "carefully assessing" whether all conditions were right for the deal to be implemented.
From proceeds of oil sales under the deal, $1,13 billion are to go on humanitarian needs, of which $260 million are to be directed at Kurds in the North.
